answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days and limits it to one bid per hour, whether buying timber, booking a ledge repair, or ordering garden supplies. Creating new names does not bypass the bond or rate limit: running 1,000 identities ties up $100,000 for a month. The system makes a sybil swarm costly in capital, though a wealthy attacker can still pay.
